subject: Harmonia preflight: VLAN provisioning, cross-connects and blockstore outline
content:
From: Alex Tan <alex.tan@harmonia.com>

Cc: Priya Sinha <priya.s@harmonia.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private cluster intake — initial network diagram + checklist

Hi Irene / Marissa,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached is our initial network diagram and the checklist our infra team put together for the on-prem private deployment. High level: we want Redwood Private deployed into our NYC colo (Equinix NY1), with a dedicated cross-connect and VPC-like segmentation. Key asks:

- Guidance on VLAN mapping and whether Redwood needs a dedicated BGP session or whether a static routed cross-connect is acceptable.
- Storage options: we're proposing a shared iSCSI blockstore (Dell/PowerStore) for model weights and an NVMe local cache on nodes for KV/prefix caches. Anything we should avoid?
- Encryption: Harmonia uses an HSM-managed KMS (Thales). We need to confirm how Redwood can integrate and what evidence you need for our security review.
- Node SKUs: we'll probably start with 4x r5-like CPU nodes + 2x A100 equivalents for inference. Want your recommended nodepool split and pod scheduling hints.

Attached: harmonia_network_diagram_v1.pdf, harmonia_preflight_checklist_v0.9.xlsx

Would appreciate a short preflight call this week if possible.

Thanks,
Alex Tan
Head of Platform Engineering
Harmonia Health

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 01 Oct 2028 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private cluster intake — initial network diagram + checklist

Alex — thanks for the diagrams and checklist, this is a great start. A few clarifying items before we schedule the call:

1) Cross-connect / routing
   - Do you anticipate us advertising customer prefixes (via BGP) from Redwood nodes, or will Harmonia route a set of VLANs into the colo and Redwood consume via private IPs? BGP is supported but requires coordination for ASNs and filtering.
   - If you prefer static routes, we typically recommend one routed VLAN per Redwood tenant (or per logical environment) to simplify ACLs and monitoring.

2) Storage & blockstore
   - Can you confirm the PowerStore exposes LUNs over iSCSI only, or do you also have an NVMe-oF path? The latter changes our recommended PV classes.
   - Do you have a retention/SLA target for model artifacts (cold tier vs warm)? That affects whether we rely on the shared blockstore or push periodic snapshots to object storage.

3) KMS/HSM
   - We'll need an admin contact and a minimal list of evidence items for the security review (KMS audit logs, access controls, key rotation policy). We can provide a template later.

4) Node sizing & workload profile
   - Can you share expected QPS/peak tokens-per-second and concurrency per model? If you don't have exact numbers, a ballpark (e.g., 2k QPS for text-gen or 200 concurrent sessions) helps us size node pools and KV cache sizing.

Proposed next steps: 30-minute intake call Wednesday or Thursday — Marissa, Karthik and Jonas will join the call to map the network and storage flow. I attached our initial preflight checklist with a few Redwood-specific columns filled in.

Best,
Irene Choi
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Private cluster intake — initial network diagram + checklist

Alex / team — quick technical note from infra side after I reviewed the diagram:

Summary recommendations (short):
- Node pools: 2 CPU-only pools for control/worker services (4x r5 equivalent each) + 2 GPU pools for inference (A100/80GB class) — split GPUs by model class (heavy vs light).
- Storage: use the PowerStore iSCSI LUNs as the persistent layer for model weights (PV class: iscsi-blockstore). For KV/prefix caches use local NVMe on each node (fast ephemeral PVs) and configure cached layers with lvm-thin on top of NVMe to allow eviction.
- Mount options: ext4/xfs tuned with noatime, nodiratime; fio profiling in preflight to choose stripe / queue depth.
- Network: prefer routed VLANs with BFD if you're doing dynamic failover. If ASNs/BGP are off the table, static routing is fine — we will use explicit firewall rules and source-based routing at the colo.
- Encryption: Redwood will integrate with your HSM via an out-of-band key-wrapping workflow for disk encryption keys. We'll need an OIDC service account for API calls to the KMS and a short PKI exchange for mTLS.

Operational caveats:
- Avoid exposing the iSCSI management plane across VLANs — keep iSCSI traffic on a dedicated storage VLAN with ACLs and MTU tuned.
- Local NVMe caches must be marked as ephemeral in our orchestration to avoid accidental persistence; we recommend labeling with node.kv-cache=true and taints to ensure only cache pods land there.
- Snapshot cadence: take model-weight backups nightly to object storage off-site. If retention is long (30+ days) consider a cheaper S3-compatible object tier for cold artifacts.

I've attached an updated preflight (column added: "redwood-actionable") and a short checklist for the colo team to run fio and iperf tests against the NVMe and storage VLAN.

Attachments: redwood_harmonia_preflight_v1.xlsx (attached to this message)

Happy to cover any of the above in the intake call.

-Karthik
